items.action_summary: Posture risk was moderate during the analyzed movement. The main opportunities are to reduce forward trunk bending and reduce deep knee flexion.

interventions.title: Protect the back
interventions.observation: Forward trunk positioning was observed repeatedly during the assessment, beyond the upright range in 6 of 29 measured frames (peak 13°). The camera was not side-on for most of the video, so forward bending may be larger than measured.
interventions.recommendation: Keep the back closer to a neutral position where practical. Reduce repeated forward bending by bringing the task closer or adjusting the work surface.

interventions.title: Reduce deep knee bending
interventions.observation: Deep knee bending was observed consistently during the assessment, in 27 of 27 measured frames (peak 107° of knee flexion).
interventions.recommendation: Where practical, raise or reposition the work area to reduce prolonged or repeated deep knee flexion.

interventions.title: Keep work within a comfortable reach
interventions.observation: Raised upper-arm positions were observed consistently during the assessment, in 29 of 29 measured frames (peak 55° from the body).
interventions.recommendation: Position frequently used work within a comfortable reach to reduce prolonged arm elevation.

interventions.title: Reduce neck bending
interventions.observation: Neck bending away from upright was observed repeatedly during the assessment, in 19 of 29 measured frames (peak 23°).
interventions.recommendation: Bring the task closer to eye level where practical and avoid prolonged downward viewing.

product_recommendations.name: BackEX
product_recommendations.headline: Evaluate BackEX for this task
product_recommendations.rationale: The assessment observed repeated forward trunk bending, beyond the upright range in 6 of 29 measured frames. Alongside improving task height, reach and work positioning, consider evaluating Extrive's BackEX support solution for tasks involving repeated or sustained bending. Review whether its intended support, fit and operating requirements match this task before introducing it.
product_recommendations.intended_use: BackEX is a passive back-support exosuit designed for repetitive lifting, forward bending and load-carrying tasks in industrial, warehousing, manufacturing and logistics work.
product_recommendations.operating_principle: It is a lightweight, fabric-based wearable with no batteries or motors. Elastic elements are tensioned as the wearer bends forward and return that stored energy as the trunk straightens, so part of the effort needed to control and reverse forward bending is shared by the suit instead of being carried by the lower-back muscles alone.
task_types: Load carrying and material handling, such as warehouse picking, parcel loading and unloading, inventory movement, assembly-line lifting and fabrication work
suitability: Confirm the task involves the repeated or sustained forward bending BackEX is designed to support.
Have a qualified person check fit, comfort and freedom of movement with the worker before regular use.
Check that it can be worn with the clothing and protective equipment the task requires.
Run a trial period and gather the worker's feedback on comfort and acceptance.
complementary_actions: Adjust the workstation and work height where practical.
Bring tools and materials closer to reduce unnecessary reaching and bending.
Avoid prolonged or repeated awkward postures where possible.
Evaluate BackEX fit, task suitability, comfort and worker acceptance before use.
product_recommendations.evidence_note: This report makes no claim about the size of any BackEX benefit. Evaluate whether it improves task comfort and work efficiency in your operating environment; Extrive can share its product evaluation material on request.
product_recommendations.qualification: This video assessment observed posture only. It does not establish that this worker needs BackEX or that it will suit them, and BackEX does not replace correcting the work design. Have a qualified person assess fit and task suitability before introducing it.
sources: Extrive BackEx scientific validation report, section 2: the BackEx exosuit and its working principle (2025)

measurement_reliability.explanation: Joint angles are estimated from 2D pose landmarks. They are most reliable when the worker is clearly visible from a side view. Oblique, rear, frontal or partly hidden views can distort the estimated angles, especially trunk lean, and may understate or overstate a posture.
measurement_reliability.title: Limited measurement reliability
reasons: The camera was close to side-on in only 3% of measured frames. Trunk lean in particular may be larger or smaller than measured.
measurement_reliability.recommendation: For a confident assessment, record a new video with the camera to the side of the worker and the whole body in view. This assessment and its results are kept as recorded.
